claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you, and I'm happy to help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask a follow-up question about his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or on an approved training course? If so, could you tell me a bit more about what he's doing (for example, is he still at school, college, or on a training programme)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 16 and not currently in full-time education or on an approved training course, I have one more question about his situation.

Has Alex recently left school (within the past 20 weeks), and has he registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation for work or training? 

Also, is Alex working more than 24 hours a week, or receiving certain benefits in his own name (such as Universal Credit or Income Support)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. And no, he's not working - or at least not anything that's 24 hours a week. He doesn't get any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Are you responsible for Alex? This means he lives with you, or you contribute towards the cost of looking after him at least the same amount as Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Is there anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And no, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 16 years old
- He is not currently in full-time education or on an approved training course
- He has not registered with a careers service or similar organisation since leaving school
- He is not working 24+ hours a week and is not receiving benefits in his own name
- You are responsible for him (he lives with you)
- You live in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Let me now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex:**
Child Benefit is normally paid for children until they turn 16. After age 16, you can continue to receive Child Benefit only if the child stays in approved full-time education or training (until they turn 20), or if they have registered with a careers service or similar organisation after leaving school.

Since Alex:
- Is 16 years old
- Is not in full-time education or approved training
- Has not registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar body

...the conditions for continuing Child Benefit are not currently met.

**What you could do:**
If Alex registers with a careers service or returns to full-time education or approved training, you may become eligible again. It might be worth encouraging Alex to register with a careers service, as this could help him find opportunities while also potentially restoring your eligibility for Child Benefit.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
